title: Why Use Radio?
description: Subscribe to [WebSocket](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455) and [Redis Pub/Sub](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/interact/pubsub/) channels from inside DuckDB SQL. Incoming messages buffer into queryable tables; outgoing messages queue with status tracking. The whole thing lives in one process — no separate consumer service, no message-queue runtime to operate.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: Radio collapses the ceremony around real-time messaging into SQL. The path from "events arriving on a WebSocket" to "rows you can `JOIN` and `WHERE` against" is one [`CALL`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/call) plus a [`SELECT`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/select).

bulletPoints.label: Listen and drain
bulletPoints.description: [`radio_subscribe`](#radio_subscribe) opens a connection; messages flow into an in-memory buffer that [`radio_received_messages`](#radio_received_messages) and [`radio_subscription_received_messages`](#radio_subscription_received_messages) expose as ordinary tables. Each message has a `seen_count` so you can drain incrementally.

bulletPoints.label: Queue and broadcast
bulletPoints.description: [`radio_transmit_message`](#radio_transmit_message) queues outbound messages. [`radio_subscription_transmit_messages`](#radio_subscription_transmit_messages) is the queue's view — pending, transmitted, or failed — so you can poll for delivery and retry from SQL.

bulletPoints.label: Inspect what's connected
bulletPoints.description: [`radio_subscriptions`](#radio_subscriptions) lists every active subscription with its endpoint and state. Useful for dashboards and `radio_*` debug queries.

bulletPoints.label: Test without the wire
bulletPoints.description: [`radio_subscription_received_message_add`](#radio_subscription_received_message_add) injects messages straight into a subscription's inbox. Lets you unit-test SQL pipelines that consume `radio_*` tables without standing up a real upstream.

sections.title: Supported transports
sections.description: Radio currently supports two transports. Additional ones are on the roadmap; the table function surface stays the same regardless of which protocol a subscription uses.

bulletPoints.label: WebSocket
bulletPoints.description: Standard [RFC 6455](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455) WebSocket client. Subscribe with a `ws://` or `wss://` URL — ideal for browser-style real-time feeds, Slack-style event streams, and custom server-sent event APIs that speak WS.

bulletPoints.label: Redis Pub/Sub
bulletPoints.description: Subscribe to one or more [Redis channels](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/interact/pubsub/) by passing a Redis URL plus channel name. For application data flows that already use Redis as the bus.

bulletPoints.label: Roadmap
bulletPoints.description: Per the [extension docs](https://query.farm/duckdb_extension_radio.html), planned protocols include Google Pub/Sub, Azure Service Bus, MQTT, and subprocess pipes. Today's transports are WebSocket and Redis Pub/Sub only.

sections.title: Production caveats
sections.description: What to know before pointing this at anything important.

bulletPoints.label: In-memory, process-scoped buffers
bulletPoints.description: Received messages live in an in-process buffer. When the DuckDB process exits, all subscriptions are torn down and unread messages are lost. For at-least-once semantics across restarts, persist drained messages to a real durable store before processing.

bulletPoints.label: Buffers are size-limited
bulletPoints.description: The received-message queue has a fixed capacity — older messages are evicted as new ones arrive. Drain with [`radio_received_messages`](#radio_received_messages) frequently enough to keep up with the inbound rate, or gate the upstream so it doesn't out-pace your reads.

bulletPoints.label: Best-effort delivery for outbound
bulletPoints.description: [`radio_transmit_message`](#radio_transmit_message) queues a message; the extension delivers it asynchronously. The per-subscription `transmit_successes`, `transmit_failures`, `transmit_last_success_time`, and `transmit_last_failure_time` columns on [`radio_subscriptions`](#radio_subscriptions) report delivery progress; [`radio_subscription_transmit_messages`](#radio_subscription_transmit_messages) shows individual queued messages.

bulletPoints.label: Single connection per subscription
bulletPoints.description: Multiple DuckDB connections in the same process don't share subscription state. Open subscriptions on the connection that will be draining them.

bulletPoints.label: Experimental status
bulletPoints.description: Function surface and parameter shapes may change. Pin a known-good extension version in production.

useCases.title: Live dashboards in DuckDB
useCases.description: Subscribe to a market-data or activity-event WebSocket and refresh a dashboard tile by re-querying [`radio_received_messages`](#radio_received_messages) on a timer. No separate consumer, no message broker.

useCases.title: SQL-driven event responders
useCases.description: Pull events with [`radio_subscription_received_messages`](#radio_subscription_received_messages), do the SQL logic, then [`radio_transmit_message`](#radio_transmit_message) the response back to a Redis Pub/Sub fanout — entirely in one query loop.

useCases.title: Ad-hoc traffic inspection
useCases.description: Point a subscription at a channel you don't yet understand, drain the inbox into a `CREATE TABLE AS`, and `GROUP BY` to discover the message shape. Faster than wiring up a custom consumer.

useCases.title: Pipeline testing
useCases.description: Use [`radio_subscription_received_message_add`](#radio_subscription_received_message_add) to inject canned messages and exercise downstream SQL exactly as it would behave on the real channel.
